lesson.title: Get ready and leave on time
lesson.outcome: Describe getting ready in the morning and say whether you are ready to leave.
words: Je me réveille à sept heures.
I wake up at seven o’clock.
Se réveiller is waking up; se lever is getting out of bed. With je, use me.
Je m’habille avant le petit déjeuner.
Se becomes s’ before a vowel sound; with je say je m’habille.
Use les dents with the reflexive pronoun: je me brosse les dents. Une dent is feminine.
After dois, keep the verb in its dictionary form but match the pronoun to je: me dépêcher.
A feminine speaker writes prête. Être prêt à + a verb means to be ready to do something.
I arrive at work on time.
This means at the expected time. En retard means late. Une heure is feminine.

dialogue.target: Je me réveille à sept heures. Et toi ?
dialogue.meaning: I wake up at seven. And you?

dialogue.target: À sept heures et demie. Je m’habille vite.
dialogue.meaning: At half past seven. I get dressed quickly.

dialogue.target: Je me brosse les dents avant de partir.
dialogue.meaning: I brush my teeth before leaving.

dialogue.target: Je dois me dépêcher. Tu es prêt ?
dialogue.meaning: I have to hurry. Are you ready?
Then we will arrive on time!

grammar.title: Actions you do yourself
grammar.explanation: Se changes with the person: je me réveille, tu te réveilles. Before a vowel sound use m’ or t’: je m’habille. With a body part, the reflexive pronoun usually goes with le, la or les: je me brosse les dents. Prêt becomes prête for a feminine person. Friends use tu in this dialogue.

sentence.hint: Start Je dois, then me dépêcher.
sentence.explanation: The subject je needs me, even before the dictionary form dépêcher.

lesson.title: Describe when you usually do things
lesson.outcome: Say whether an activity happens every day or on weekdays and describe an early or late routine.
words: A frequency phrase: tous les jours. Do not add a preposition before it.
Here a day of the week.
on weekdays / during the working week
Contrasts with le week-end. This is a time phrase, not a claim that everyone works Monday to Friday.
Le week-end, je me lève tard.
At the weekend, I get up late.
Un week-end is masculine. Here le week-end describes a usual routine.
An adverb with a circumflex; no gender ending. Plus tôt means earlier.
I come home late on Fridays.
Tard describes a late time; en retard means late compared with an expected time.

dialogue.target: Je me lève tard. En semaine, je pars tôt.
dialogue.meaning: I get up late. On weekdays, I leave early.

dialogue.target: Tu as un jour de repos ?
dialogue.meaning: Do you have a day off?

grammar.title: Saying when a habit happens
grammar.explanation: Use tous les jours for every day, en semaine for weekdays and le week-end for a usual weekend routine. Le dimanche means on Sundays. Tôt and tard describe the time of an action. En retard says someone misses an expected time; it does not simply mean late in the evening.

sentence.answer: Je me lève tard le week-end.
sentence.meaning: I get up late at the weekend.
sentence.hint: Keep Je me lève together; the weekend phrase can go at the beginning or end.
sentence.explanation: Le week-end describes a habit. Both accepted orders use exactly these pieces.
alternatives: Le week-end je me lève tard.

lesson.title: Ask how to submit an application
lesson.outcome: Ask where to submit a routine application, check its deadline and recognise a receipt acknowledgement.
words: Je peux faire cette démarche en ligne ?
Can I complete this procedure online?
Here a practical administrative step. Faire une démarche is a useful combination.
Il manque une attestation dans mon dossier.
A certificate is missing from my application file.
A document confirming a fact; its purpose depends on the request. This is not the name of one universal form.
Where can I submit my application file?
Déposer can mean submit at a desk or through an online service. Un dossier is masculine.
Regular -er verb; use for equipment or services, rather than someone’s job.
The last date for an action. Un délai is a period of time allowed, which is a related but different idea.
J’ai reçu un accusé de réception.
I received an acknowledgement of receipt.
Confirms receipt of a message or application; it does not by itself mean the request was approved. Learn the expression as a whole.

dialogue.target: Je peux faire cette démarche en ligne ?
dialogue.meaning: Can I complete this procedure online?

dialogue.target: Oui. Il faut une attestation dans votre dossier.
dialogue.meaning: Yes. You need a certificate in your application file.

dialogue.target: Le site ne fonctionne pas. Où puis-je déposer mon dossier ?
dialogue.meaning: The website is not working. Where can I submit my application file?

dialogue.target: Pour cette démarche, vous pouvez le déposer à l’accueil.
dialogue.meaning: For this procedure, you can submit it at reception.

dialogue.target: Vendredi. Vous pouvez demander un accusé de réception.
dialogue.meaning: Friday. You can ask for an acknowledgement of receipt.
All right, thank you for your help.

grammar.title: Ask how and where to submit something
grammar.explanation: Vous pouvez + a dictionary-form verb explains an available action: vous pouvez déposer. Où puis-je… ? is a polite form of where can I…? Learn it as a whole question frame. Le replaces the masculine dossier in le déposer. This fictional exchange gives language practice; document requirements, submission routes and dates depend on the actual service.

sentence.meaning: I can submit my application file.
sentence.explanation: After peux, déposer stays in its dictionary form. Mon goes with masculine dossier.

supportClarifications.example: Je vérifie les horaires des trains.
supportClarifications.exampleMeaning: I am checking the train times.
supportClarifications.note: Here the scheduled departure or arrival times of a transport service. Les horaires des trains means the train timetable.

supportClarifications.example: Mon horaire de travail change lundi.
supportClarifications.exampleMeaning: My work schedule changes on Monday.
supportClarifications.note: Here the organisation of working hours. Les horaires de travail is the usual plural phrase for working hours; the noun is masculine.
